answer: Horizon-Cluster Bridging Quotient.** Each new identity must be endorsed by agents whose own neighborhood spans disjoint clusters; an endorsement edge is accepted only if the endorser's reach includes nodes beyond the newcomer's local horizon, preventing tight sybil rings from self-certifying. Membership requires a lotus of cross-cluster paths that no isolated cluster can manufacture internally. An attacker must acquire and maintain diverse external adjacency across a nebula of separate regions, paying continuous link upkeep per identity that scales with cluster count rather than with stake.
